rationale: Static SimpleDateFormat instances are shared by concurrent web requests and are not thread-safe.
The field is initialized to null, never assigned, and exposed by a getter; register() instead assigns an unused local trackingId.
The DTO exposes getNextLocation(), but no constructor or method writes the field.
Locale-explicit formatting is useful but lower priority than the thread-safety defects and broadens the initial cleanup.
Locale-explicit case conversion is useful but is a separate compatibility cleanup.
Catching NullPointerException hides the actual invalid input or state and merits later focused cleanup.
The equals implementation contains a redundant or misplaced null check and merits later focused cleanup.
JSF passivation behavior requires container-context review before treating this as a defect.
The JPA/domain object pattern requires review before changing constructor behavior.
The Jakarta WebSocket container owns Session lifecycle; application code removes sessions on close rather than closing each after send.
The checkpoint code intentionally combines assignment and condition evaluation.
